thread:
Olivia (Support): hey team — AcmeOps is hitting a spike of 5xx/gateway timeouts on hosted inference endpoints since ~08:05 UTC. They report ~40% requests 502/504. Customer is escalating. ticket #INC-8324. Can oncall triage?

Raj (Oncall): on it. I can see elevated 504s in gateway logs for tenant acmeops-prod. Latency to backend pods is high and we have a backlog. Opening k8s dashboard. :eyes:

Marta (Eng-SRE): throwing preliminary hypothesis: scale-up lag. KEDA scaledobject shows activationThreshold=100, pollingInterval=30s, cooldownPeriod=300s. If traffic came in sudden burst from Acme, scaler might be slow to react. Any warmup hooks configured for model containers?

Ken (Eng-Runtime): runtime teams — our model pods take ~45s to cold-start for that model (gpt-mini-fp16) due to weight init and kv cache priming. We rely on readiness probe that waits for /healthz to respond. If KEDA only scales after activationThreshold and poll interval, combined delay can cause gateway timeouts.

Ava (Infra): checking cluster autoscaler and nodepool. Node pool has max surge room but I see some pending provisioning in GCP zone europe-west1-b — 2 nodes provisioning now (started ~08:06). Could be slow zone allocation during this burst.

Olivia (Support): customer says they sent a one-off big training job that spiked E2E traffic (unexpected). They are asking for ETA and root cause. Also they saw failed billing auth around the same time — could that interact?

BillingBot: note — a short-lived billing auth token failure for acmeops at 08:04:31 (returned 401), retried and succeeded at 08:04:34. No ongoing billing blocks.

Raj (Oncall): timeline I'm stitching: 08:04 — billing auth hiccup but retried ok; 08:05 — massive traffic burst; 08:06 — KEDA sees metric later due to 30s poll; 08:06-08:07 — nodes provisioning; 08:07-08:08 — pods scheduling + model init; lots of requests hit gateway between 08:05-08:09 -> 504. Seems like classic scale-up stall.

Ken (Eng-Runtime): quick mitigation: can we add an emergency temporary fallback to a cheaper warm model variant for acmeops-prod? We have a smaller quantized variant that boots in ~8s — compatible outputs. If we route new requests there, reduce error rate while infra catches up.

Marta (Eng-SRE): agree. Options: 1) manual horizontal scale of deployment to N replicas (kubectl scale) to drain queue; 2) patch KEDA to lower activationThreshold and pollingInterval for this tenant ScaledObject; 3) route traffic to variant model. Which do we want to run right now?

Raj (Oncall): I'm going to manually scale replicas to 6 for acmeops-prod model svc. Running:
```
kubectl -n hosted-inference scale deployment acmeops-model-gpt --replicas=6
kubectl get pods -l app=acmeops-model-gpt -n hosted-inference -w
```

DeployBot: scale action queued by raj. New pods scheduled: model-gpt-5, model-gpt-6.

Ava (Infra): node provisioning finished; 2 nodes ready. Pods are scheduling. Watching readiness probes — a few are failing initial /healthz due to long init times.

Ken (Eng-Runtime): while scale helps, readiness probe is still waiting for KV cache priming. We can reduce readiness timeout to accept traffic earlier with degraded but still useful responses — risky. Alternative: enable warmup container that populates weights before marking ready. That change needs a deployment commit.

Marta (Eng-SRE): for immediate relief let's do two steps: 1) patch scaledobject for acmeops to pollingInterval=5 and activationThreshold=20 (temporary), 2) set frontend route fallback to model-gpt-quantized for acmeops until we stabilize. I'll prepare the KEDA patch.

Raj (Oncall): temporary routing change:
```
# route update via router-admin
routerctl route set acmeops-prod --model model-gpt-quantized --weight 50
```
Applying now.

Olivia (Support): messaging to customer: "we've identified autoscaling lag due to combined KEDA polling + node provisioning + model cold-starts. We're applying temporary routing to a faster quantized variant and adjusting autoscaler settings. ETA for stabilization ~5–10m. Sorry for the disruption — we'll follow up with a root cause and remediation plan." Customer acknowledged and appreciates fast updates.

Ella (Customer: AcmeOps): thanks team. Please confirm SLA credits/compensation path. We hit production users.

Olivia (Support): filing for credits per SLO escalation. cc @billing.

BillingBot: created billing case BC-4432 for potential SLA credit evaluation, linked to INC-8324.

Marta (Eng-SRE): KEDA patch applied (pollingInterval -> 5s, activationThreshold -> 20) for acmeops ScaledObject. We'll revert after traffic normalizes. Monitor shows scaler reacting within a single poll now.

Ken (Eng-Runtime): router change applied and verified. Quantized variant serving ~60% of new requests for acmeops. Error rate dropped from 42% -> 7% in last 3 mins. Logs:
```
[08:12:03] gateway: 502 backends=14/20 backlog=89
[08:14:10] gateway: 200 backends=18/18 backlog=12
```

Raj (Oncall): marking incident as mitigated. Still treating as P1 until we revert patches and confirm no regression. Need follow-ups:
- Eng-Runtime: propose readiness/warmup change or pre-warm hooks for heavy models (Ken)
- Eng-SRE: review KEDA defaults (Marta) — activationThreshold 100 and poll 30s are too conservative for bursty tenants
- Infra: review nodepool cold-start SLA and placement (Ava)
- Support/Billing: customer follow-up and credits (Olivia)

Marta (Eng-SRE): creating action item ticket AE-1294: "KEDA defaults & warmup strategy for hosted inference" with repro notes + metrics + suggested remediation.

Ken (Eng-Runtime): also adding runbook snippet for emergency routing to quantized variants + safety checks to avoid silent quality regressions.

Olivia (Support): customer updated and will wait for writeup. They requested a postmortem and a timeline for permanent fix. I told them we'll have a follow-up within 48h.

Ella (Customer: AcmeOps): appreciate it. Please include details on why billing auth briefly failed earlier; it coincided with the start of the burst.

Raj (Oncall): billing auth looks like transient upstream token provider latency; not blocking. We captured logs and included in AE-1294.

Olivia (Support): closing until postmortem. Thanks all :heart:

DeployBot: incident INC-8324 status -> mitigated; mitigations: manual scale, KEDA patch, route fallback.

Marta (Eng-SRE): last note — consider tenant-level throttles and burst-protection (queueing with graceful degradation) so a single tenant burst doesn't exhaust shared routing buffer. Adding to AE-1294.
